card.line: Lebanon is a mountain region north of Israel, famous for its cedar trees, which Solomon and later the returning exiles used to build God's temple.

moments.title: Solomon asks for cedars
moments.text: Solomon asks King Hiram of Tyre to have cedars of Lebanon cut for the Lord's house. Hiram agrees, and his servants haul the logs from Lebanon to the sea.

moments.title: Israelite workers sent to Lebanon
moments.text: Solomon sends 10,000 men at a time to Lebanon in monthly shifts. They spend one month there and two months at home.

moments.title: House of the Forest of Lebanon
moments.text: Solomon builds a great palace hall called the House of the Forest of Lebanon. It has four rows of cedar pillars holding up cedar beams.

moments.title: The thistle and the cedar
moments.text: King Jehoash of Israel answers Amaziah with a story about a thistle and a cedar in Lebanon. A wild beast tramples the thistle, and Jehoash warns Amaziah not to stir up trouble.

moments.title: Cedar for the second temple
moments.text: The returned exiles pay people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar logs from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. Cyrus king of Persia had authorized this.
